Official Events & Updates
23rd November 2026
SNID November 2026 — Chakwal Passes All Six LQAS Lots

Alhamdulillah, all six LQAS (Lot Quality Assurance Sampling) lots in District Chakwal passed with a Pass/High result in the Sub-National Immunization Days (SNID) campaign of November 2026. The successful passing of all lots is proof of the entire team's hard work, dedication and excellent performance.

"Alhamdulillah! The successful passing of all LQAS lots in District Chakwal is proof of the entire team's hard work, dedication and excellent performance. On this remarkable achievement, all UCMOs, AICs and frontline polio workers deserve congratulations and special tribute. Your tireless efforts are commendable. In recognition of your services, Appreciation Letters will be issued. May Allah Almighty grant you all further success. Ameen!"
— Dr. Ali Ammar, District Health Officer, Chakwal

Congratulations to the SNID Team
We are thankful to Allah Almighty that we have successfully conducted the Polio vaccination campaign under the guidance of CEO DHA, DHO (PS) and DPO WHO. Congratulations to all UCMOs, AICs and frontline workers of District Chakwal on the completion of the SNID campaign, achieving high scores in the pre-campaign MPQA, the post-campaign LQAS and the Market Survey.

It was definitely a difficult campaign, as in this Sub-National Campaign Chakwal was included as a Risk district at the eleventh hour, with shortage of time, HR constraints, a high number of seasonal MMP and a 6-month gap since the last campaign. Despite this, all the management, UC supervisors and frontline workers accepted the challenge and completed the campaign victoriously.

Special appreciation for:
  • Asma Jabeen, UCMO Kot Sarang
  • Khizar Hayat, UCMO T.M Khan-II
  • Shamas Shah, UCMO Chakwal 3
  • Naheed Kausar, UCMO Mureed
  • Ansar Mehmood, UCMO Choa Saidan Shah
  • Faheem Razaq, UCMO Kallar Kahar
  • and their AICs, along with the other UCs.
Passing LQAS in Choa Saidan Shah is the biggest achievement, as there are 900 MMP in the UC and it is very difficult to cover them. However, all managed it very well, with excellent coverage by supervisors and frontline workers.

The efforts of Master Trainers, ASVs, MP validators, DEOs and all other stakeholders are also appreciated.

Insha'Allah, we will continue to work in upcoming campaigns with the same zeal, zest and spirit, and will try to fulfil all the gaps and deficiencies highlighted in this campaign. Together we can eradicate Polio from Pakistan.
23rd November 2026
Deputy Commissioner Reviews Polio Campaign; Certificates of Appreciation Distributed

A meeting chaired by Deputy Commissioner Chakwal, Ms. Sarah Hayat, was held to review the previous polio campaign and to prepare for the next polio campaign starting in mid-December. During the previous campaign, Chakwal successfully cleared all samples tested, Alhamdulillah.

On the occasion, Certificates of Appreciation were distributed among officers and UCMOs for their excellent performance, and necessary instructions were issued for the effective preparation and success of the upcoming campaign.
18th August 2026
WHO Divisional Officer Dr. Tariq Saleem Visits Chakwal to Review EPI and VPD Surveillance

Dr. Tariq Saleem, Divisional Officer at the World Health Organization (WHO), conducted an extensive official visit to District Chakwal to evaluate and strengthen local healthcare operations.

During his visit, Dr. Saleem carried out a detailed assessment of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (VPD) Surveillance and the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI). He identified critical operational gaps and provided strategic guidance to healthcare staff on effective rectification measures to improve overall performance.

As part of his itinerary, Dr. Saleem inspected DHQ Hospital Chakwal, focusing on:
  • Ice-Lined Refrigerators (ILRs) to ensure strict cold chain maintenance.
  • Monitoring Charts to verify precise record-keeping.
  • QR Code & Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Integration to assess digital tracking efficiency.
Addressing the Lady Health Visitors (LHVs), Dr. Saleem emphasized the crucial role of complete data accuracy, instructing them to ensure 100% data entry compliance across both QR code systems and EMR portals without delay.

EPI MIS vs EMR — UC-wise Comparison

Source: EPI-MIS Consolidated UC-wise Report (January–October 2026) compared with EMR outreach records (HMIS Child Immunization Outreach Report, January–November 2026 sheets). EMR doses are counted by dose date for January–October 2026; duplicate child records are removed (latest record per MR number; 97,528 children from 121,862 records). Comparison covers the 20 child antigens common to both reports (HPV and Td are not recorded in EMR). EMR holds outreach records only, while EPI-MIS is the consolidated total, so the two are not expected to match exactly. The With Fixed Site tab adds Fixed Site doses to EMR outreach for a combined comparison against the same consolidated EPI-MIS total. Difference = EMR − EPI-MIS; % Difference = Difference ÷ EPI-MIS × 100. UCs are listed tehsil-wise: Chakwal, Choa Saidan Shah, Kallar Kahar, Talagang.

Source: EMR Outreach entries (same data as Outreach Reports). Select a date to get that day's verification call list — narrow it with the Tehsil and UC filters to view one UC's children only. Tap Dial to call the parent/guardian — on a PC connected to your mobile with Phone Link, the call goes through your mobile. After each call, tap one status button; statuses save automatically and sync to all your devices through the cloud — a status set on one laptop or mobile appears on every other device. Download the day's Excel file (with statuses) any time with the button above the list. You can also attach an Additional Comment to any child — comments save with the record and are included in the Excel download. Tip: click any summary box above the list (Total Children, Verified, Not Responding, …) to filter the list to just those children.

Tehsil-wise Summary — Drop-out Rates

District Chakwal | High drop-out: >+10% or <−2% between consecutive doses

Tehsil Avg BCG→P1 Avg P1→P3 Avg MR1→MR2 UCs with High DO (>10%)
Chakwal +4.9% −2.0% +10.5% 36
Choa Saidan Shah −33.4% −11.0% +10.3% 8
Kallar Kahar −40.8% −220.8% +10.2% 9
Talagang −18.4% −33.3% +19.7% 29
Key Observations
  • Chakwal is relatively better on BCG→P1 and P1→P3; MR1→MR2 drop-out still high (+10.5%).
  • Kallar Kahar shows extreme P1→P3 anomaly (−220.8%) — likely data quality / reporting issue; needs urgent verification.
  • Choa Saidan Shah & Talagang have high drop-out across BCG→P1 and P1→P3 pathways.
  • Total UCs with high drop-out (>10%): 82 (Chakwal 36 + Talagang 29 + Kallar Kahar 9 + Choa 8).
  • Action: Investigate defaulters, session quality, and data anomalies in high-DO UCs.
Note: High drop-out is defined as >+10% or <−2% between consecutive doses. Negative values often indicate catch-up vaccination or data inconsistency.
